answer: Idena's synchronous ceremony makes each extra identity pay one live human solving flips in two minutes; a farm running N fakes pays N humans at the same minute and cannot share it because one mind cannot sit two ceremonies at once. Every two weeks all answer as one, each flip a picture story ordered from a whisper of context, needing 60% to pass. A relic of the password era: copies count for nothing; the kernel is simultaneity. One solver on two seats dies by the clock at 2: the second seat's flips expire unsolved, its stake forfeited.
